assumptions: The specific trigger for the division by zero (a zero or empty monthly-spend denominator) is inferred from the error type and the code path the flag enables; no code or stack trace was inspected to confirm it.

The incident's recorded end time reflects escalation to humans, not confirmed recovery. The last log line read, at 22:51, still shows the flag evaluating 'on' and ZeroDivisionErrors continuing, so we assume the fault was still active at handover.

The mitigation is assumed to have mis-applied rather than been ineffective: the change log records the flag being set back to 'on' at 22:50:43, and flag evaluation logs are treated as ground truth over the flag provider's own history, which the automation read as showing only one recent change.
The low, intermittent UpstreamTimeout errors present before 22:42 are treated as pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident.
Impact is assumed confined to the account page; no other endpoint or service was examined, and no downstream or upstream dependency was checked.
Who or what turned the flag on, and whether it was an intentional rollout, was never established — no owner or change ticket was retrieved.
The steady 200 flag evaluations per minute across the whole window is taken at face value as the service's traffic on this path; no independent traffic measurement was consulted.
input.executive_summary:
Shortly before 23:00 UTC on 15 September 2026, a newly switched-on feature on the online shop's account page began failing for a portion of customers trying to view their accounts. The failure started the moment the feature was enabled and continued for the rest of the incident window; customers hitting it saw the account page error rather than load. Nothing had been released or deployed — the only change was the feature being turned on.

Automated response picked the incident up within seconds and correctly identified the newly enabled feature as the cause. It then attempted to undo the change, but that attempt did not take effect: the change record shows the feature being set back to *on*, and the service's own logs continued to report the feature as on and the same errors continuing after the action. The automation judged its own fix to have failed, re-investigated, arrived at the same conclusion, and escalated to humans roughly five minutes after the first alert with the fault still live and the corrective action — genuinely disabling the feature and confirming the service reports it as off — not yet performed. Customer impact was therefore ongoing at the point of handover, and the recorded impact figures for this incident come from the shop's own measurements, not from this review.
input.root_cause: At 22:42 the feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was switched from off to on for io-shop (ramping in-minute: 61 off / 139 on, fully on from 22:43), and the account-page code path it enables raises `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` — almost certainly an empty or zero monthly-spend denominator — so a sustained share of account page renders failed from that minute onward. The onset aligns minute-for-minute with the flag flip and no deploy or release is recorded for the service anywhere in the preceding week, which rules out a code change as the trigger; the defect is latent in the already-deployed build and was merely exposed by the flag.
